paragraphs: On Friday morning, Tom and Ben stood on the platform at the train station. Their class was going to visit a toy factory in the next town. Teacher Nick bought all the tickets himself. "I like trains," said Ben. "In my opinion, a train is better than a bus, because it has no traffic." "I agree," said Tom. "And the seats are more comfortable."

Then the speaker over the platform spoke. "The ten o'clock train is delayed by twenty minutes." "Twenty minutes!" said Ben. "We will be late." "Don't worry, children," said Teacher Nick. "The factory will wait for us." Tom looked at the big map on the wall. "We can take a bus from the station," he said. "The bus stop is just outside."

"I don't think so," said Ben. "In my opinion, the bus is slower, because there is a lot of traffic in the morning." "But a bus leaves now, and the train is late," said Tom. Teacher Nick walked to the information desk to ask for details. "Excuse me," he said to the woman at the desk. "Would you tell me the details of our train?" "It leaves at twenty past ten from platform three," she said. "It stops at four stations, and the ride takes half an hour." "Then we will wait," said Teacher Nick.

The train came at twenty past ten, and the children got on. Tom and Ben sat next to the window and watched the green fields. At the factory, a man in a blue coat met them at the gate. "Welcome," he said. "I will show you how we make toy cars." In a big room, a machine cut a round piece of wood. "This will be a wheel," said the man. "It is still warm," said Tom, and he touched it.

Each child painted a small wooden wheel. Ben painted his wheel blue, and Tom painted his wheel red. "In my opinion, this is the best part of the trip," said Tom. On the way home, the train was on time. "See?" said Ben. "The train is better." Tom laughed. "Okay," he said, "you are right this time."
